record.paper_title: Opportunities and open questions in modern β decay
record.original_question: How large are second-order isospin-symmetry-breaking corrections to the nucleon vector charge gV, can coherent sums over excited T = 1/2 and T = 3/2 nucleon states make them several parts in 10^-4 rather than the naive 10^-5 scale, and can lattice calculations determine the correction with below-10^-4 theory uncertainty?

evidence.quote: Strong interaction isospin breaking effects arise from quark mass differences, so that corrections to gV were initially estimated to be of order ( mu − md)2/Λ2 QCD ∼ 10−5, i.e. beyond the current experimental precision.

Recent work, however, has cast some doubt upon this claim as some authors find corrections on the order several parts in 10−4, depending on their model of choice (101). Such an effect would directly translate into shifts of the Vud value for all extractions on the order of its current uncertainty estimate, and be of significant importance.

Enhancements such as those found in Ref. (101) can then be understood as a coherent sum of individual excited states, thereby exceeding the simple power counting result. These may be calculated on the lattice directly, so that a large theory uncertainty on the non-perturbative calculation should result in a theory uncertainty below 10 −4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider semileptonic neutron β decay, in which the nucleon vector coupling g_V appears in the hadronic matrix element of the charged weak current. In the exact isospin limit (equal up and down quark masses, no electromagnetism), the conserved-vector-current hypothesis fixes g_V = 1. Strong-interaction isospin-symmetry breaking, generated by the quark mass difference (m_u − m_d), induces a correction Δg_V whose leading nonzero contribution is of second order in isospin breaking and naive power counting in chiral effective theory gives

   Δg_V ~ (m_u − m_d)^2 / Λ_QCD^2 ~ 10^{-5}.

However, an estimate based on a sum over intermediate excited nucleon states (T = 1/2 resonances such as Roper-like states and T = 3/2 Δ-like states) coupled coherently through the isospin-violating part of the QCD Hamiltonian could in principle exceed the naive power-counting estimate.

Address the following:

(a) Derive, within a hadronic representation of the vector current matrix element, an expression for Δg_V as a coherent sum over excited T = 1/2 and T = 3/2 nucleon intermediate states, and determine whether this sum can yield |Δg_V| at the level of several parts in 10^{−4}, rather than 10^{−5}.

(b) Determine whether a first-principles lattice QCD calculation of the same matrix element, including isospin-breaking quark-mass insertions and the full tower of intermediate states, can be performed with a total (statistical plus systematic) theory uncertainty on Δg_V below 10^{−4}.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature confirms ongoing debate: hadronic-model estimates (e.g., based on coherent sums over excited nucleon states) yield isospin-breaking corrections to g_V at the several-parts-in-10^{-4} level, contradicting the naive 10^{-5} power-counting estimate. No published lattice QCD calculation has yet delivered Δg_V with sub-10^{-4} controlled uncertainty; the question remains open as of recent reviews and lattice efforts.

status_evidence.title: Isospin Breaking in the Nucleon Mass and the Sensitivity of β Decays to New Physics
status_evidence.snippet: Estimates corrections to g_V from quark mass differences potentially exceeding naive power counting.
status_evidence.claim: Hadronic-model estimates suggest Δg_V can be larger than the 10^-5 naive estimate.

status_evidence.title: Isospin breaking in the vector current of the nucleon
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses isospin-breaking contributions to the nucleon vector current matrix element.
status_evidence.claim: The size of Δg_V remains under active theoretical investigation.

status_evidence.title: Precision determination of nucleon iso-vector scalar and tensor charges at the physical point
status_evidence.snippet: Recent lattice QCD calculations of nucleon iso-vector charges at sub-percent precision but not yet at 10^-4 for vector-charge isospin-breaking corrections.
status_evidence.claim: Lattice precision below 10^-4 on Δg_V has not been achieved.
